title: Cistern token bucket
object: Close-coupled WC cistern with a diaphragm float valve and a pull-knob drop valve, in section
idea: Token bucket rate limiting (API rate limits)
summary: The water is the tokens. A fixed Ø3.5 jet at mains pressure refills at 0.146 L/s whatever the level, which is a constant token rate, and the float shuts it at capacity. Each pull of the knob takes one 1.5 L dose; below one token the dose float rests on its stop and the pull is refused, and the overflow tube is the hard cap if the float is held down.
usedFor: Explaining API rate limits, bursts and HTTP 429 in a software-concepts course
A physical analogy for token bucket and leaky bucket algorithms in system design teaching
Plumbing training: diaphragm float valves, orifice flow and Torricelli drain
controls: Pull (click or drag up) the knob or Space sends a request · H holds the float down (overflow) · R refills · S slow motion
